newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall as long-term bond yield nears 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall as long-term bond yield nears 7 pct.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell on Thursday as long-term bond yields neared 7 percent, a level that could draw investment money away from equities.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 27.61 points at 7,263.08.
But in the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a thin margin on active volume of 246 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 2.99 points at 1,370.76.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 11/32, which raised its yield to 6.99 percent from Wednesday's 6.96 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"Everyone is focused on the bond yield," said Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt.
"As long as the long bond stays below 7 percent, the stock market should be all right," he said. "If it moves above that, the market could see some trouble."
Bonds grew more nervous about inflation after the government reported Wednesday that the U.S. trade gap narrowed sharply in March, while exports and imports soared to a record high.
The inflation jitters spilled over into the stock market, which was worrying about future interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve, which on Tuesday opted to keep monetary policy unchanged.

The strong trade numbers fanned concern that the government might have to revise upward its estimate of 5.6 percent first-quarter growth, which would boost the odds that the Fed would raise interest rates to slow the economy's growth.

"Faced with rising exports and a weaker dollar, bonds could sell off and test the 7.25 percent level," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management unit. "If bonds go the other way, stocks, which are fully-discounting calendar 1997 earnings, could retrace ..."
While blue-chip stocks fell, the shares of smaller-name companies fared better.
"We've seen some broad participation in smaller companies," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.
Among individual stocks, RCSB Financial Inc. rose six points to 40 following an announcement that it would be acquired by Charter One Financial Inc. in a $635 million stock deal.
CFM Technologies Inc. fell 9-3/8 to 28 after the company said aggressive pricing would hurt its results for the remainder of the year.
